extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and recipients of NIH grants (institutions, investigators, authorized organizational representatives), including research administrators and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards NIH-funded applicants and recipients must follow to manage clinical trials, confidentiality, controlled substances, debarment/suspension, reporting, information security, and financial conflict of interest compliance under NIH terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial regulatory responsibilities by responsible party status
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on whether the NIH-funded clinical trial is an applicable clinical trial under the regulation and whether the recipient is the responsible party, the recipient must ensure all regulatory requirements are met or coordinate with the responsible party; if not an applicable clinical trial under the regulation, the recipient is responsible for carrying out tasks and meeting timelines described in regulation (including registering the trial in ClinicalTrials.gov and submitting results information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three cases: (1) If trial is applicable and recipient is responsible party — ensure regulatory requirements are met. (2) If trial is applicable but recipient is not responsible party — coordinate with responsible party to ensure requirements are met. (3) If trial is not an applicable clinical trial — recipient must still register the trial in ClinicalTrials.gov and submit results as described in regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent form public posting requirement (45 CFR 46.116(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each funded trial that is non-exempt human subjects research subject to the revised Common Rule and that meets the definition of a clinical trial, one IRB‑approved consent form must be posted on a designated public federal website after recruitment closes and no later than 60 days after the last study visit by any subject, as required by the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH-funded recipients using English-language forms may submit an IRB-approved English-language informed consent form to ClinicalTrials.gov (follow ClinicalTrials.gov upload instructions; ClinicalTrials.gov does not currently support non-English documents) or submit to Regulations.gov following instructions. Recipients submitting to Regulations.gov must maintain the Regulations.gov receipt/tracking number and make it available to NIH upon request. Recipients using only non-English forms must submit to Regulations.gov per OHRP guidance. All submissions must protect participant privacy consistent with applicable laws (e.g., HIPAA, Certificates of Confidentiality) and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single ClinicalTrials.gov record per NIH-funded clinical trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NIH-funded clinical trial should have only one entry in ClinicalTrials.gov containing its registration and results information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients need not and should not create a separate record of the applicable clinical trial to comply with NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA Amendments Act (FDAAA) registration and results submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarize with 42 U.S.C. 282(j) (Sec. 801 of Public Law 110-85) and 42 CFR Part 11 requirements for registration and submission of results information that apply to certain clinical trials; results information for applicable clinical trials are generally due not later than 12 months after the primary completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the primary completion date occurs after the period of performance has ended, results submission is still required according to FDAAA and award terms. The Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) signature on the grant/progress report certifies that for applicable clinical trials funded by the award the responsible party has made all required registrations and results submissions under 42 CFR Part 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Cause Extension (GCE) request submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: GCE requests for clinical trial results deadlines must be submitted through the ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration and Results System (PRS) prior to (i.e., the day before) the standard submission deadline or a previously granted extended deadline; late submissions or requests outside PRS will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCEs may be sought for ACTs subject to the Final Rule (42 CFR 11.42) and NIH clinical trials subject to NIH's complementary policy. More than one GCE may be submitted for the same trial after a previous GCE was granted; when a GCE is granted the results deadline is updated to align with the approved extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCE request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each GCE request must include a complete description of the reason(s) why clinical trial results information cannot be provided by the deadline, with sufficient detail to justify good cause and allow evaluation, and an estimated date on which results will be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient detail should include steps that will be taken to meet the estimated submission date, mitigation steps to avoid future delay, and any other information needed to address evaluation criteria. Requests that lack sufficient information may be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCE evaluation criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: GCE requests will be evaluated case-by-case using general criteria including: (1) circumstances and their impact and mitigation steps; (2) extent to which factors are outside the responsible party's control; (3) what will be done during the extension and why those steps are necessary and whether the requested date is commensurate; (4) internal consistency with relevant data element definitions and other sections of the study record; and (5) number/explanations for previous GCEs and prior proposed reporting deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria are illustrative and not exhaustive; NIH may consider other relevant information when determining whether 'good cause' exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCE formatting and submission considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: GCE requests must be in English, spell out acronyms/abbreviations at first use, and should not include specific personal health information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should provide clear, organized information; failure to follow these formatting considerations may impede review.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCE appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible parties or recipients may appeal denied GCE requests or an NIH-identified earlier deadline specified in a granted extension; an appeal must explain why the initial decision was incorrect and cannot present new bases for extension for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one appeal may be submitted for a denied GCE request, via PRS not later than 30 calendar days after the PRS notification date. NIH will notify whether the appeal is granted or denied; if granted, submit results by the extended date in the notification; if denied, submit results by the later of the original due date or 30 calendar days after the denial notification. Appeals that present new bases will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic issuance and scope of Certificates of Confidentiality (CoC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of Confidentiality are issued automatically to any NIH-funded investigators or institutions engaged in biomedical, behavioral, clinical, or other research activities in which identifiable, sensitive information is collected or used (per subsection 301(d) of the PHS Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates protect identifiable, sensitive information collected and all copies, in perpetuity. Certificates issued automatically are not provided as separate documents; institutions/investigators are responsible for determining whether their research is subject to the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of research covered by CoCs
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH considers research to be covered by CoCs if it involves human subjects research as defined in 45 CFR Part 46 (including some exempt research unless subjects cannot be identified), collection/use of biospecimens identifiable to an individual or with even a very small risk of re-identification, generation/use of individual-level human genomic data, or any other research where there is at least a very small risk that combination of information could deduce identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should assess whether their activity is biomedical/behavioral/clinical research and then whether it meets any of the listed conditions; a 'yes' to any triggers the CoC protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoC disclosure prohibitions and permitted disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients issued a Certificate shall not disclose or provide in any Federal, State, or local civil, criminal, administrative, legislative, or other proceeding the name of an individual or information/documents/biospecimens that contain identifiable, sensitive information created or compiled for the research, unless disclosure is made with the individual's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is permitted only when: required by Federal/State/local laws (with exceptions noted), necessary for medical treatment with the individual's consent, made with the individual's consent, or made for other scientific research that complies with applicable Federal human subjects protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibilities for CoCs and internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are required to establish and maintain effective internal controls (e.g., policies and procedures) to provide reasonable assurance that award management complies with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms; institutions must ensure non-NIH-funded investigators or institutions receiving CoC-protected data understand they are subject to subsection 301(d) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are responsible for ensuring subrecipients that receive copies of identifiable sensitive information understand they are subject to the CoC requirements; NIH expects investigators to inform participants of CoC protections and limits when informed consent is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections for substance use patient records (42 CFR Part 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 543 of the PHS Act implemented in 42 CFR Part 2 requires records of substance abuse patients to be kept confidential except under specific circumstances and purposes; these protections differ from HIPAA and are intended to protect patients from increased vulnerability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered records include any information of a patient who has applied for or been given diagnosis/treatment for substance use at a federally assisted program, including identity, diagnosis, or treatment maintained in connection with performance of substance abuse education, training, treatment, rehabilitation, or research under an NIH grant. Except as authorized by a court order, patient records may not be used to initiate/substantiate criminal charges or investigations of a patient. Regulations describe procedures allowing nonvoluntary disclosure of certain information by persons engaged in mental health research, including substance use research.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIPAA Privacy Rule applicability and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information (Privacy Rule) govern protection of individually identifiable health information; decisions about applicability and implementation of the Privacy Rule reside with the researcher and recipient organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provides decision tools and educational materials (e.g., 'Protecting Health Information in Research: Understanding the HIPAA Privacy Rule') to help determine whether an entity is subject to the rule; recipients should consult OCR resources for guidance specific to grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled substances research compliance (DEA requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If controlled substances are proposed to be administered as part of a research protocol or research is conducted on the substances themselves, applicants/recipients must ensure DEA requirements (registration, inspection, certification, as applicable) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional DEA offices provide forms and information regarding the type of registration required; NIH references NIDA and DEA contacts for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and suspension obligations (2 CFR Part 376 / Part 180)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of NIH grants must determine whether they or any principals are excluded or disqualified prior to entering into covered transactions (i.e., prior to drawdown of funds) and report to the funding IC if they or principals are excluded, convicted of listed offenses within preceding three years, indicted/charged, or had public transactions terminated or defaulted within three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may check SAM but are not required to. Disclosure of unfavorable information will not necessarily cause denial; NIH will consider disclosures and explanations. Failure to disclose known information may lead to termination for material failure or other remedies such as suspension and debarment. Recipients must immediately report new qualifying information discovered during the project period (including no-cost extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower-tier transaction (subaward/contractor) debarment checks and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier transactions (consortiums, subcontracts, consultants, contractors with goods/services ≥ $25,000) are subject to the HHS debarment/suspension regulations; recipients must verify lower tier participants are not excluded and must require lower-tier participants to comply and pass the requirement further down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not enter into a lower tier transaction with a disqualified person unless an exception is obtained from HHS. Lower-tier participants must report to the recipient if they or participants are excluded or disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-Free Workplace Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the AOR agrees the recipient will provide a drug-free workplace and comply with the requirement to notify NIH if an employee is convicted of violating a criminal drug statute; failure to comply may be cause for debarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-wide requirements are found in 2 CFR Part 182; HHS implementing regulations are in 2 CFR Part 382. Foreign applicants/recipients may be exempted based on documented finding by the NIH awarding IC that application is inconsistent with international obligations or foreign laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) recipient reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: FFATA requires full disclosure of entities receiving Federal funds via USASpending.gov; two recipient reporting obligations are: information on executive compensation (when not reported elsewhere) and information on all subawards/subcontracts/consortiums over $30,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USASpending includes awardee name, award amount, FAIN, funding agency, location, unique identifier, and names/compensation of highly-compensated officers (as applicable). Recipient reporting details are in NIH Monitoring—Reporting—Financial Reports—Recipient Reporting of Subrecipient Data for FFATA; full award term at 2 CFR Part 170.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: FISMA protections apply to information systems, electronic or hard copy, that contain Federal data; applicability to NIH recipients applies only when recipients collect, store, process, transmit, or use information on behalf of HHS or any component organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other cases FISMA is not applicable to recipients of grants. The recipient retains original data and IP and is responsible for security subject to applicable laws; when information collected by a recipient is provided to HHS, responsibility for protection of the HHS copy transfers to HHS and HHS must protect it as required by FISMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) institutional process requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires recipient institutions (except Phase I SBIR/STTR applicants/recipients) to comply with 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart F and maintain an up-to-date, written and enforced administrative process to identify and manage FCOI for all research projects for which PHS funding is sought or received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overarching goal is to promote objectivity and avoid bias in design, conduct, or reporting of PHS-funded research. The institution must promote and enforce investigator compliance with disclosure requirements and review SFIs to determine relatedness to NIH-funded research. A FCOI exists when the institution reasonably determines the SFI could directly and significantly affect design, conduct, or reporting of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI reporting content and mechanism (initial and annual reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an institution determines an FCOI exists it must report to the NIH awarding IC via the eRA Commons FCOI Module, submitting an initial FCOI report containing specified elements and annual FCOI reports thereafter within the competitive segment or until the FCOI no longer exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial report elements include: grant number and PD/PI, name of Investigator with FCOI, entity name, nature of the FCOI (e.g., consulting fees, equity), value categories ($0-4,999; $5,000-9,999; $10,000-19,999; $20,000-100,000 by $20,000 increments; above $100,000 by $50,000 increments or statement if value cannot be determined), description of how the interest relates to the research and basis for the institution's FCOI determination, and key elements of the management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI management plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Key elements of the institution's management plan that must be reported include: (1) role and principal duties of the conflicted Investigator, (2) conditions of the management plan, (3) how the plan safeguards objectivity, (4) confirmation of the Investigator's agreement to the plan, (5) how the plan will be monitored to ensure compliance, and (6) other information as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements must be part of the initial report and used to monitor and enforce the plan; annual reports must include status of the FCOI and changes to the management plan, if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI subrecipient written agreement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must enter into a formal written agreement with each consortium participant and/or subrecipient that establishes whether the recipient's FCOI policy or the subrecipient's policy will apply and must include required SFI disclosure, review, and FCOI reporting timelines to ensure compliance with FCOI regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subrecipient institutions that rely on their own FCOI policy must report identified FCOIs to the recipient in sufficient time to allow the recipient to meet NIH reporting obligations. NIH will not support agreements that do not meet minimum requirements; if a subrecipient refuses the agreement, the agreement cannot be issued. NIH may request copies of written agreements and supporting documentation; failure to provide requested documentation may lead to noncompliance remedies and enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of certain FCOI information
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must make certain information available concerning identified FCOI held by senior/key personnel via a publicly accessible website or by written response within five business days of a request, and update such information as specified in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution's FCOI policy must be up-to-date, written, enforced, publicly accessible, and submitted to NIH via the eRA Commons Institution Profile (IPF) Module. The public posting requirement applies at the institutional level not grant-specific level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator disclosure obligations, including foreign financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must require each Investigator (and spouse/dependent children) to disclose domestic and foreign Significant Financial Interests (SFIs) related to institutional responsibilities; investigators must disclose foreign financial interests (including income from seminars, lectures, advisory committees, and reimbursed/sponsored travel) when such income meets the disclosure threshold (e.g., income in excess of $5,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are strongly encouraged to review their FCOI policies and make necessary changes to ensure investigators fully understand disclosure responsibilities. Disclosed SFIs must be reviewed to determine relatedness to NIH-funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI training requirement for investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Each institution must require each Investigator (including subrecipient Investigators) to complete FCOI training prior to engaging in NIH-supported research and at least every four years, and immediately under designated circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated circumstances triggering immediate retraining are set by regulation (e.g., policy revisions, noncompliance, or new investigator participation); institutions must track and enforce training timelines.
